records.literal_gloss: And a woman, one of [the] wives of [the] sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha, saying, Your servant, my husband, [is] dead, and you know that your servant was fearing Yahweh; and the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves.

en.L: And a woman from the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
en.B: The wife of a man from the company of prophets cried out to Elisha, "My husband, your servant, has died, and you know that your servant feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Now the man he owed money to has come to take my two children as his slaves."
en.R: A woman whose husband had been one of the group of prophets cried out to Elisha for help. She said, "My husband, your servant, has died. You know how he honored and obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But now a man my husband owed money to has come to take my two boys away to be his slaves."

es.L: Y una mujer de entre las mujeres de los hijos de los profetas clamó a Eliseo, diciendo: «Tu siervo, mi marido, ha muerto, y tú sabes que tu siervo temía {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Y el acreedor ha venido a llevarse a mis dos hijos para que sean sus esclavos».
es.B: La viuda de uno de los discípulos de los profetas clamó a Eliseo: «Mi marido, tu siervo, ha muerto, y tú sabes que tu siervo temía {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Ahora el hombre a quien le debía dinero ha venido a llevarse a mis dos hijos como esclavos».
es.R: Una mujer cuyo marido había sido del grupo de profetas le pidió ayuda a gritos a Eliseo. Le dijo: «Mi marido, tu siervo, ha muerto. Tú sabes cómo honraba y obedecía {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Pero ahora un hombre al que mi marido le debía dinero ha venido a llevarse a mis dos hijos para hacerlos sus esclavos».

fr.L: Et une femme d’entre les femmes des fils des prophètes cria vers Élisée en disant : « Ton serviteur, mon mari, est mort, et tu sais que ton serviteur craignait {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et le créancier est venu prendre mes deux enfants pour [en faire] ses esclaves. »
fr.B: La femme d’un des disciples des prophètes implora Élisée : « Mon mari, ton serviteur, est mort, et tu sais que ton serviteur craignait {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et maintenant, l’homme à qui il devait de l’argent est venu prendre mes deux enfants pour en faire ses esclaves. »
fr.R: Une femme dont le mari avait fait partie du groupe de prophètes a appelé Élisée au secours. Elle lui a dit : « Mon mari, ton serviteur, est mort. Tu sais combien il respectait {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et lui obéissait. Mais maintenant, un homme à qui mon mari devait de l’argent est venu prendre mes deux garçons pour en faire ses esclaves. »

sw.L: Na mwanamke mmoja wa wake za wana wa manabii akamlilia Elisha, akisema, "Mtumishi wako, mume wangu, amekufa, nawe unajua kwamba mtumishi wako alikuwa akimcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Na sasa mdai amekuja kuwachukua watoto wangu wawili wawe watumwa wake."
sw.B: Mke wa mtu mmoja wa kundi la manabii alimlilia Elisha, akasema, "Mume wangu, mtumishi wako, amekufa, nawe unajua kwamba mtumishi wako alimcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Sasa mtu aliyekuwa akimdai amekuja kuwachukua watoto wangu wawili wawe watumwa wake."
sw.R: Mwanamke mmoja ambaye mumewe alikuwa mmoja wa kundi la manabii alimlilia Elisha aombe msaada. Akasema, "Mume wangu, mtumishi wako, amekufa. Unajua jinsi alivyomheshimu na kumtii {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Lakini sasa mtu ambaye mume wangu alikuwa na deni lake amekuja kuwachukua wavulana wangu wawili wawe watumwa wake."

vi.L: Có một người đàn bà trong số các vợ của các con trai của các nhà tiên tri kêu van với Ê-li-sê: "Đầy tớ của ông, chồng tôi, đã chết, và ông biết đầy tớ của ông kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Nay chủ nợ đến để bắt hai đứa con tôi làm nô lệ cho ông ta."
vi.B: Vợ của một người trong đoàn tiên tri kêu van với Ê-li-sê: "Chồng tôi, là đầy tớ của ông, đã qua đời, và ông biết đầy tớ của ông vẫn kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Nay người chủ nợ đến để bắt hai đứa con tôi làm nô lệ cho mình."
vi.R: Có một người đàn bà mà chồng từng ở trong đoàn tiên tri, đến kêu cứu với Ê-li-sê. Bà nói: "Chồng tôi, là đầy tớ của ông, đã qua đời. Ông biết anh ấy hết lòng kính sợ và vâng lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Nhưng bây giờ người mà chồng tôi mắc nợ đến để bắt hai đứa con trai tôi đem về làm nô lệ."

ko.L: 그리고 예언자의 아들들의 아내들 가운데 한 여자가 엘리사에게 부르짖어 말했다. "어른의 종인 제 남편이 죽었습니다. 그리고 어른의 종이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 경외했다는 것을 어른께서 아십니다. 그런데 빚쟁이가 제 두 아이를 자기 종으로 데려가려고 왔습니다."
ko.B: 예언자 무리에 속한 사람의 아내 하나가 엘리사에게 부르짖었다. "어른의 종인 제 남편이 죽었습니다. 어른께서도 아시다시피, 어른의 종은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 경외하던 사람이었습니다. 그런데 남편에게 돈을 빌려준 사람이 와서 제 두 아이를 종으로 데려가려고 합니다."
ko.R: 예언자 무리에 속했던 사람의 아내가 엘리사에게 도와 달라고 부르짖었다. "어른의 종인 제 남편이 죽었습니다. 어른께서도 아시다시피, 제 남편은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 공경하고 그분의 말씀을 따랐습니다. 그런데 남편이 돈을 빌린 사람이 와서 제 두 아들을 데려가 자기 종으로 삼으려고 합니다."

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets: members of a community of prophets
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means members of a group, not children. Such groups of prophets lived at Bethel, Jericho and Gilgal (2 Kings 2:3, 5, 15; 4:38) and looked to Elisha as their leader (6:1). Some of them, like this woman's husband, were married and had families.

decisions.choice: your servant: a humble way of speaking of her husband as Elisha's loyal follower
decisions.reason: Speaking of someone as "your servant" to a person of higher standing was the polite way to address him (Genesis 18:3; 1 Samuel 20:7-8). It reminds Elisha that the dead man belonged to his own circle.

decisions.choice: feared the LORD: lived in reverence and obedience toward Yahweh
decisions.reason: To fear Yahweh is to honor him and keep his ways (Deuteronomy 10:12). She names her husband's faithfulness as the ground of her appeal: a godly man's family is now about to be broken up.

decisions.choice: the creditor came to take her children as slaves: enslavement for debt
decisions.reason: A family that could not pay a debt could lose its children to the lender as slaves until the debt was worked off. The law limited this and required release for Israelites (Exodus 21:2-7; Leviticus 25:39-43; Deuteronomy 15:12), but the prophets show how harshly it was used (Amos 2:6; Nehemiah 5:5). For a widow, losing her sons meant losing her only support.

decisions.choice: slaves (every level)
decisions.reason: Here the children are to be taken as property in payment of a debt, so enslavement itself is the point. Following the style guide, "slave" stays at every level instead of "servant".

decisions.choice: company of prophets (Balanced); group of prophets (Readable)
decisions.reason: These are the book-wide wordings for "sons of the prophets". Balanced and Readable also make clear that her husband was the member of the group.

decisions.choice: honored and obeyed
decisions.reason: Readable explains "feared" by what it meant in practice, so a young reader does not think he was afraid of God.

decisions.choice: esclavos (every level)
decisions.reason: The children are to be taken as property in payment of a debt, so slavery itself is meant and "esclavo" stays at every level, as the Pentateuch note has for slaves bought and sold.

decisions.choice: honraba y obedecía
decisions.reason: Readable explains "feared" by what it meant in practice, as the English does, so that no one reads it as being afraid of God.

decisions.choice: "esclaves" at every level
decisions.reason: Enslavement for debt is the point of the story, so French keeps "esclaves" at every level, as the English does and as the French style guide asks where slavery itself is meant.

decisions.choice: "watumwa" at every level
decisions.reason: The children are to be taken as property for a debt, so slavery itself is the point and "mtumwa" stands at every level, as the Swahili notes set for slaves bought and sold.

decisions.choice: the widow calls Elisha "ông" and herself "tôi"; Elisha calls her "bà"
decisions.reason: A woman of the prophets' community speaks to their leader with respect but as one of his own people.

decisions.choice: The widow speaks to Elisha in 합쇼체, calling him "어른" and her husband "어른의 종"
decisions.reason: A woman asking a prophet for help speaks with the highest respect; "어른" is the address these drafts use for a respected prophet (2:16, 19).

decisions.choice: "종" for the slaves the creditor would take, at every level
decisions.reason: The Genesis note keeps "종" for *ʿeved* and uses "노예" only where slavery itself is meant; here the debt-slavery is clear from "take ... as", and "종" keeps the link with "your servant" earlier in the verse.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֤יהָ אֱלִישָׁע֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ הַגִּ֣ידִי לִ֔י מַה־יֶּשׁ־לָ֖ךְ בַּבָּ֑יִת וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֣ין לְשִׁפְחָתְךָ֥ כֹל֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת כִּ֖י אִם־אָס֥וּךְ שָֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Elisha, What shall I do for you? Tell me, what is there to you in the house? And she said, There is not to your maidservant anything in the house except a flask of oil.

en.L: And Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a flask of oil."
en.B: Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what is there in your house?" She replied, "Your servant has nothing at all in the house, except a small jar of oil."
en.R: Elisha asked her, "How can I help you? Tell me, what do you have at home?" She answered, "I have nothing in the house except a little jar of olive oil."

es.L: Y Eliseo le dijo: «¿Qué haré por ti? Dime, ¿qué tienes en casa?». Y ella dijo: «Tu sierva no tiene nada en casa, sino una vasija de aceite».
es.B: Eliseo le dijo: «¿Qué puedo hacer por ti? Dime, ¿qué tienes en tu casa?». Ella respondió: «Tu sierva no tiene nada en casa, excepto un frasco pequeño de aceite».
es.R: Eliseo le preguntó: «¿Cómo te puedo ayudar? Dime, ¿qué tienes en casa?». Ella respondió: «No tengo nada en casa, solo un frasquito de aceite de oliva».

fr.L: Et Élisée lui dit : « Que ferai-je pour toi ? Dis-moi, qu’as-tu à la maison ? » Et elle dit : « Ta servante n’a rien du tout à la maison, sinon une fiole d’huile. »
fr.B: Élisée lui dit : « Que puis-je faire pour toi ? Dis-moi, qu’as-tu dans ta maison ? » Elle répondit : « Ta servante n’a rien du tout à la maison, sauf une petite fiole d’huile. »
fr.R: Élisée lui a demandé : « Comment puis-je t’aider ? Dis-moi, qu’est-ce que tu as chez toi ? » Elle a répondu : « Je n’ai rien à la maison, sauf une petite fiole d’huile d’olive. »

sw.L: Elisha akamwambia, "Nikufanyie nini? Niambie, una nini nyumbani?" Akasema, "Mjakazi wako hana kitu chochote nyumbani isipokuwa chupa ya mafuta."
sw.B: Elisha akamwambia, "Nikufanyie nini? Niambie, una nini nyumbani mwako?" Akajibu, "Mtumishi wako hana kitu chochote nyumbani, isipokuwa kichupa kidogo cha mafuta."
sw.R: Elisha akamwuliza, "Nikusaidieje? Niambie, una nini nyumbani?" Akajibu, "Sina kitu chochote nyumbani isipokuwa kichupa kidogo cha mafuta ya zeituni."

vi.L: Ê-li-sê nói với bà: "Tôi sẽ làm gì cho bà? Hãy nói cho tôi biết, bà có gì trong nhà?" Bà nói: "Tớ gái của ông chẳng có gì trong nhà cả, ngoài một bình dầu."
vi.B: Ê-li-sê hỏi bà: "Tôi có thể làm gì cho bà? Hãy cho tôi biết, trong nhà bà có gì?" Bà đáp: "Đầy tớ của ông chẳng có gì trong nhà cả, ngoài một hũ dầu nhỏ."
vi.R: Ê-li-sê hỏi bà: "Tôi có thể giúp bà thế nào? Hãy cho tôi biết, bà có gì ở nhà?" Bà trả lời: "Tôi chẳng có gì trong nhà ngoài một hũ dầu ô-liu nhỏ."

ko.L: 그리고 엘리사가 그에게 말했다. "내가 너에게 무엇을 해 주랴? 너의 집에 무엇이 있는지 내게 말하여라." 그러자 그가 말했다. "이 여종의 집에는 기름 한 병 말고는 아무것도 없습니다."
ko.B: 엘리사가 그에게 말했다. "내가 너를 위해 무엇을 해 줄 수 있겠느냐? 네 집에 무엇이 있는지 말해 보아라." 그 여자가 대답했다. "이 여종의 집에는 기름 한 병밖에 아무것도 없습니다."
ko.R: 엘리사가 물었다. "내가 어떻게 도와주면 좋겠느냐? 네 집에 무엇이 있는지 말해 보아라." 그 여자가 대답했다. "저희 집에는 올리브기름이 든 작은 병 하나밖에 아무것도 없습니다."

decisions.choice: a flask of oil: a small container of oil
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It seems to come from a verb meaning to pour oil on or anoint, so it was probably a small flask of oil for the skin, not a storage jar. Either way she has almost nothing.

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a humble way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: A woman speaking to someone of higher standing called herself "your maidservant" (1 Samuel 1:16; 25:24). She speaks as a petitioner.

decisions.choice: you: an older written form of the feminine "you", read in the usual way
decisions.reason: In this chapter the written Hebrew several times keeps an older spelling of the feminine "you" and "your" (here and in verses 3, 7, 16 and 23), and the traditional reading gives the usual form. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: your servant (Balanced); I (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the polite self-reference as "your servant"; "maidservant" sounds dated. Readable says simply "I".

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: The oil of Israel was olive oil; Readable names it, as 1 Kings 17:12 does.

decisions.choice: tu sierva (Literal, Balanced); yo (Readable)
decisions.reason: The polite self-reference is "tu sierva" at Literal and Balanced, as "tu siervo" in Samuel; Readable says simply "yo", as the English says "I".

decisions.choice: "mjakazi wako" (Literal); "mtumishi wako" (Balanced); first person (Readable)
decisions.reason: A woman's humble "your maidservant" follows the Swahili Samuel drafts: "mjakazi" at Literal, the neutral "mtumishi" at Balanced, and plain "mimi" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "tớ gái của ông" (L); "đầy tớ của ông" (B); "tôi" (R)
decisions.reason: A humble way of saying "I" (m2), in the terms note's forms for a woman speaking.

decisions.choice: Elisha speaks to the widow in the plain style (해라체); she calls herself "이 여종" (L, B), "저" (R)
decisions.reason: The widow of one of the prophets' company comes to Elisha as to her husband's master; the plain style of a prophet to a disciple's household fits, as Elijah speaks to Elisha. "이 여종" follows the Samuel note's "이 종" for humble self-reference.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִ֨י שַׁאֲלִי־לָ֤ךְ כֵּלִים֙ מִן־הַח֔וּץ מֵאֵ֖ת כָּל־שְׁכֵנָ֑יִךְכֵּלִ֥ים רֵקִ֖ים אַל־תַּמְעִֽיטִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Go, borrow for yourself vessels from the outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not make few.

en.L: And he said, "Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not get [only] a few.
en.B: He said, "Go around and borrow containers from all your neighbors, empty ones, and not just a few.
en.R: Elisha said, "Go to all your neighbors and borrow empty jars from them. Get as many as you can.

es.B: Él le dijo: «Ve y pide prestadas vasijas a todos tus vecinos, vasijas vacías, y no pocas.
es.R: Eliseo le dijo: «Ve a casa de todos tus vecinos y pídeles prestadas vasijas vacías. Consigue todas las que puedas.
